newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: QUESTION-MARK OVER PROPOSED BOTSWANA COLLIERY.
newsitem.headline: QUESTION-MARK OVER PROPOSED BOTSWANA COLLIERY.

text.p: The viability of a proposed 80 million pula colliery over the Mmamabula coalfield in Botswana has been questioned by sources in the region's coal and energy industries.

Ribson Gabonowe, Botswana's Mining Commissioner, confirmed at the weekend that a preliminary mining application had been received by Makgadikgadi Investments, but said a lot of work remained to be down.

Makgadikgadi Investments said the main customer for the colliery was expected to a power station -- although such new station is not yet a definite part of Botswana's planning nor a confirmed part of the southern Africa power pool.
Coal would hopefully also be sent 1,500 km to South Africa's iron ore plant at Saldanha Bay, it added.
In addition, South African power utility Eskom's
Matimba power station could also source 2.5 million tonnes of coal a year from the colliery, which would be 90 km from Matimba, although not directly linked to Botswana by rail.

Managing director of Makgadikgadi, Jock Burden, speaking from Johannesburg, said the company had applied for a mining lease to establish the colliery at the town of Mmamabula, 140 km north of the Botswana capital, Gaborone.

"I have a strong feeling we will be in production next year," Burden said. "One million tonnes of high quality steam coal and some metallurgical coal will be produced in the first year, rising to several million tonnes per year."

Burden said Iscor Mining, the South African mining company and subsidiary of steel giant Iscor , which operates in the adjacent Waterberg coalfield in South Africa, had been invited to participate in the venture. "We are stalling other investors, waiting for Iscor," he said.

However, Iscor Mining general manager Jannie Grimes expressed reservations. "We looked at it, but were not interested, mainly because of the logistics. The field is too far from the markets. It would not be viable," he said.
"If a power station is built on the field, that might change the picture as regards the steam coal."
